title: Organic foods: Are they safer? More nutritious?
summary: Mayo Clinic overview: organic food means less pesticide residue but unclear nutrition or health benefits; produce intake matters most.

assertions.quote: The organic food label says more about how an item was farmed than about the food itself.
Organic doesn't automatically mean the food has more nutrients.
Getting the suggested amount of fruits and vegetables every day is more important than choosing those that are organic or conventionally farmed.
Organic food exposes people to less pesticide residue than does conventionally grown food.
Aside from lessened contact with pesticides, proven links between health and organic food are less clear.
People who are pregnant might benefit from eating organic food.
Organic ingredients may be added to processed products that are high in calories, sodium or added sugar.
Both organic and conventionally grown food can be contaminated with bacteria
Taken as a whole, organic food tends to be more expensive than conventional food.
products must have more than 95% certified organic ingredients
That means at least 70% of the ingredients are certified as organic.
other terms, such as natural, aren't certified in the United States and don't mean the same thing as organic
